children.text:
śrīHarṣadeva-viracitā |
|| Priyadarśikā ||
children.translated_text:
Composed by <s>Śrī Harṣadeva</s>.
|| <s>Priyadarśikā</s> ||

children.text: dhūma-vyākula-dṛṣṭir indu-kiraṇair āhlāditākṣī punaḥ
children.translated_text: Her gaze disturbed by smoke, her eyes again delighted by the rays of the moon,

children.text: paśyantī varam utsukānata-mukhī bhūyo hriyā brahmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: looking at her chosen lord with face eagerly bowed, then again with the modesty of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: serṣyā pāda-nakhendu-darpaṇa-gate Gaṅgāṃ dadhāne hare
children.translated_text: jealously gazing at <s>Gaṅgā</s> reflected in the toenail-moons of <s>Hara</s>,

children.text: sparśād-utpulakā kara-graha-vidhau Gaurī śivāyāstu vaḥ // HPri_1.1 //
children.translated_text: her hair standing on end from his touch at the moment of taking her hand — may <s>Gaurī</s> be auspicious for you! // HPri_1.1 //

children.text:
api ca |
Kailāsādrāv udaste paricalati gaṇeṣūllasat-kautukeṣu
kroḍaṃ mātuḥ Kumāre viśati viṣa-muci prekṣamāṇe sa-roṣam /
pādāvaṣṭambha-sīdad-vapuṣi Daśamukhe yāti pātāla-mūlaṃ
children.translated_text: when <s>Daśamukha</s> (Ten-faced one), his body sinking under the pressure of his foot, is driven to the netherworld's depths,

children.text: kruddho 'py āśliṣṭa-mūrtir bhaya-ghanam Umayā pātu tuṣṭaḥ Śivo naḥ // HPri_1.2 //
children.translated_text: though angered, embraced in bodily form by <s>Umā</s> out of intense fear — may <s>Śiva</s>, thus pleased, protect us! // HPri_1.2 //

And further:
On damp <s>Kailāsa</s>, as the <s>Gaṇas</s> move about with exuberant curiosity, when <s>Kumāra</s> enters the lap of his mother while the serpent looks on angrily,

children.text:
(nāndy-ante sūtradhāraḥ parikramya) | adyāhaṃ vasantotsave sa-bahu-mānam āhūya
nānā-dig-deśād āgatena rājñaḥ śrī-Harṣadevasya pāda-padmopajīvinā rāja-samūhenoktaḥ yathāsmat-svāminā śrīHarṣadevenāpūrva-vastu-racanālaṃkṛtā Priyadarśikā nāma

nāṭikā kṛtety asmābhiḥ śrotra-paraṃparayā śrutam | na tu prayogato dṛṣṭā |
tat tasyaiva rājñaḥ sarva-jana-hṛdayāhlādino bahu-mānād asmāsu cānugraha-buddhyā
yathāvat prayogena tvayā nāṭayitavyeti | tad yāvan nepathya-racanāṃ kṛtvā yathābhilaṣitaṃ saṃpādayāmi | parito 'valokya | āvarjitāni sāmājika-manāṃsīti me niścayaḥ | kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: but we have not seen it performed. Therefore, out of great respect for that very king who delights the hearts of all people, and out of a desire to bestow favor upon us, you should properly stage it in performance.' So let me arrange the backstage preparations and accomplish what is desired. (Looking around on all sides.) I am certain that the minds of the audience are captivated. For what reason?

(After the <s>nāndī</s>, the stage-manager walks about.) Today, at the spring festival, I was respectfully summoned by a gathering of kings who have come from various regions and directions, and who subsist upon the lotus-feet of King <s>Śrī Harṣadeva</s>. They said: 'We have heard through a chain of listeners that our lord <s>Śrī Harṣa</s> has composed a <s>nāṭikā</s> (one-act play) called <s>Priyadarśikā</s>, adorned with an unprecedented arrangement of subject matter,

children.text: śrī-Harṣo nipuṇaḥ kaviḥ pariṣad apy eṣā guṇa-grāhiṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Harṣa</s> is a skilled poet, and this assembly too is one that appreciates merit,

children.text: loke hāri ca Vatsarāja-caritaṃ nāṭye ca dakṣā vayam /
children.translated_text: the story of <s>Vatsarāja</s> is charming in the world, and we are skilled in dramatic art;

children.text: vastv ekaikam apīha vāñchita-phala-prāpteḥ padaṃ kiṃ punar
children.translated_text: even a single one of these factors would be sufficient ground for attaining the desired fruit — how much more so when,

children.text: mad-bhāgyopacayād ayaṃ samuditaḥ sarvo guṇānāṃ gaṇaḥ // HPri_1.3 //
children.translated_text: by the abundance of my good fortune, this entire collection of virtues has come together! // HPri_1.3 //

children.text:
(nepathyābhimukham avalokya) | aye | kathaṃ prastāvanābhyudyate mayi viditāsmad-abhiprāyo 'ṅgādhipater Dṛḍhavarmaṇaḥ kañcukino bhūmikāṃ kṛtvāsmad-bhrāteta evābhivartate | tad yāvad aham apy anantara-bhūmikāṃ saṃpādayāmi |
(iti niṣkrāntaḥ) |
(iti prastāvanā) |
children.translated_text:
(Looking toward the backstage area.) Ah! How is it that, as I am about to begin the prologue, someone who knows my intention has assumed the role of the chamberlain of King <s>Dṛḍhavarman</s> of <s>Aṅga</s> and is approaching as though he were my own brother? Let me then take up the next role myself.
(He exits.)
(Thus ends the prologue.)

children.text:
prathamo 'ṅkaḥ |
(tataḥ praviśati kañcukī |)
children.translated_text:
Act One.
(Then enters the chamberlain.)

children.text: kañcukī - (sa-śoka-śramaṃ nāṭayan | niḥśvasya) | kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ kaṣṭam |
children.translated_text: Chamberlain — (Acting out grief and fatigue. Sighing.) Alas! Alas!

children.text: rājño vipad-bandhu-viyoga-duḥkhaṃ deśa-cyutir durgama-mārga-khedaḥ /
children.translated_text: The king's calamity, separation from dear ones, the sorrow, exile from one's country, the weariness of impassable roads —

children.text: āsvādyate 'syāḥ kaṭu-niṣphalāyāḥ phalaṃ mayaitac cira-jīvitāyāḥ // HPri_1.4 //
children.translated_text: I taste this fruit of my long life, which is bitter and fruitless. // HPri_1.4 //

children.text: (sa-śokaṃ sa-vismayaṃ ca) | tādṛśasyāpi nāmāpratihata-śakti-trayasya Raghu-Dilīpa-Nala-tulyasya devasya Dṛḍhavarmaṇo mat-prārthyamānāpy anena sva-duhitā Vatsarājāya datteti baddhānuśayena Vatsarājo bandhanān na nivartata iti ca labdha-randhreṇa sahasāgatya Kaliṅga-hatakena vipattir īdṛśī kriyata iti yat satyam upapannam api na śraddadhe | katham ekānta-niṣṭhuram īdṛśaṃ ca daivam asmāsu | yena sāpi rājaputrī yathā-kathaṃcid enāṃ Vatsarājāyopanīya svāminam an-ṛṇaṃ kariṣyāmīti matvā mayā tādṛśād api pralaya-kāla-dāruṇād avaskanda-saṃbhramād apavāhya devasya Dṛḍhavarmaṇo mitra-bhāvānvitasyaivāṭavikasya nṛpater Vindhyaketor gṛhe sthāpitā satī snānāya nātidūram ity Agastya-tīrthaṃ gate mayi kṣaṇāt kair api nipatya hate Vindhyaketau rakṣobhir iva nirmānuṣī-kṛte dagdhe sthāne na jñāyate kasyām avasthāyāṃ vartata iti | nipuṇaṃ ca vicitam etan mayā sarvaṃ sthānam | na ca jñātaṃ kiṃ tair eva dasyubhir nītāthavā dagdheti | tat kiṃ karomi manda-bhāgyaḥ | (vicintya) | aye | śrutaṃ mayā bandhanāt paribhraṣṭaḥ Pradyota-tanayām apahṛtya Vatsarājaḥ Kauśāmbīm āgata iti |

kiṃ tatraiva gacchāmi | (niḥśvasyātmano 'vasthāṃ paśyan) | kim iva hi rājaputryā vinā tatra gatvā kathayiṣyāmi | aye | kathitaṃ cādya mama Vindhyaketunā -- mā bhaiṣīḥ | jīvati tatra-bhavān mahā-rājo Dṛḍhavarmā gāḍha-prahāra-jarjarī-kṛto baddhas tiṣṭhati | iti | tad adhunā svāminam eva gatvā pāda-paricaryayā jīvita-śeṣam ātmanaḥ saphalayiṣyāmi (parikramyordhvam avalokya) | aho atidāruṇatā śaradātapasya | yad evam aneka-duḥkha-saṃtāpitenāpi mayā tīkṣṇo 'vagamyate |
children.translated_text: Shall I go there then? (Sighing, and looking at his own condition.) But what shall I say there without the princess? Ah! And <s>Vindhyaketu</s> told me today — 'Do not fear! His Majesty the great king <s>Dṛḍhavarman</s> is alive; though badly wounded by heavy blows, he remains bound.' So now let me go to my master and devote the remainder of my life to serving his feet. (Walking about and looking upward.) Oh, the fierceness of the autumn sun! For even I, scorched by so many sorrows, find it unbearable.

(With grief and astonishment.) That even such a lord as <s>Dṛḍhavarman</s>, whose three powers were irresistible, who was the equal of <s>Raghu</s>, <s>Dilīpa</s>, and <s>Nala</s> — that such a disaster should befall him! For that wretch of <s>Kaliṅga</s>, finding an opening because <s>Vatsarāja</s> would not return from captivity — harboring resentment that his own daughter, though sought by him, was given to <s>Vatsarāja</s> at my request — suddenly attacked and wrought such ruin! Truly, though it is logical, I cannot believe it. How can fate be so utterly cruel to us? For that princess too — thinking 'I shall discharge my debt to my master by somehow conveying her to <s>Vatsarāja</s>' — I rescued her even from that terrible onslaught, dreadful as the end of an age, and placed her in the house of the forest king <s>Vindhyaketu</s>, who was bound in friendship to lord <s>Dṛḍhavarman</s>. But while I had gone to the <s>Agastya</s> pilgrimage site, which was not far away, for bathing, in an instant some men fell upon and slew <s>Vindhyaketu</s>, depopulated the place as if by demons, and set it ablaze — and I do not know in what condition she is. I have thoroughly searched this entire area. I could not determine whether she was carried off by those bandits or perished in the fire. What shall I, wretched in fortune, do? (Reflecting.) Ah! I have heard that <s>Vatsarāja</s>, having escaped from captivity and carried off the daughter of <s>Pradyota</s>, has returned to <s>Kauśāmbī</s>.

children.text: ghana-bandhana-mukto 'yaṃ kanyā-grahaṇāt paraṃ tulāṃ prāpya /
children.translated_text: Released from the dense bondage of clouds, having passed beyond the seizing of the maiden into the sign of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra),

children.text: ravir adhigata-sva-dhāmā pratapati khalu Vatsarāja iva // HPri_1.5 //
children.translated_text: the sun, having attained his own splendor, blazes forth — indeed, just like <s>Vatsarāja</s>! // HPri_1.5 //

children.text:
(iti niṣkrāntaḥ) |
(iti viṣkambhakaḥ) |
children.translated_text:
(He exits.)
(Thus ends the interlude.)

children.text:
(tataḥ praviśati rājā vidūṣakaś ca) |
rājā -
bhṛtyānām avikāritā parigatā dṛṣṭā matir mantriṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The steadfastness of servants has been tested, the minds of ministers observed,

children.text: mitrāṇy apy upalakṣitāni viditaḥ paurānurāgo 'dhikam /
children.translated_text: friends too have been recognized, the affection of the citizens known even more;

children.text: nirvyūḍhā raṇa-sāhasa-vyasanitā strī-ratnam āsāditaṃ
children.translated_text: the passion for daring in battle has been fully carried through, the jewel among women obtained —

children.text: nirvyājād iva dharmataḥ kim iva na prāptaṃ mayā bandhanāt // HPri_1.6 //
children.translated_text: as if through sheer righteousness, without pretense — what indeed have I not gained from captivity? // HPri_1.6 //

(Then enter the king and the <s>vidūṣaka</s>.)
The King —

children.text: vidūṣakaḥ - (sa-roṣam) | bho vassa | kahaṃ taṃ evva dāsīe uttaṃ bandhaṇa-hadaaṃ pasaṃsesi | taṃ dāṇiṃ visumaridaṃ | jaṃ taha ṇava-ggaho via gaa-vaī khala-khalāamāṇa-loha-siṅkhalābandha-paḍikkhalanta-calaṇo suṇṇa-dukkhara-pisuṇida-hiaa-saṃdāvo rosa-vas'-uttambhida-diṭṭhī gurua-kara-phoḍia-dharaṇi-maggo raaṇīsu vi aṇiddā-suhaṃ aṇuhūdo si |
children.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s> — (Angrily.) My dear friend! Why do you praise that very wretch of captivity, that son of a slave-woman? Have you forgotten already? How, like a newly captured lordly elephant, stumbling in your chains of clanking iron fetters, the anguish of your heart betrayed by your empty trunk-like face, your gaze stiffened by suppressed rage, your path on the ground pounded by heavy shackles — even in the nights you experienced the pleasure of sleeplessness!

children.text: bho vayasya | kathaṃ tam eva dāsyāḥ putraṃ bandhana-hatakaṃ praśaṃsasi | tad idānīṃ vismṛtam | yat tathā nava-graha iva gaja-patiḥ khala-khalāyamāna-loha-śṛṅkhalābandha-pratiskhalac-caraṇaḥ śūnya-mukha-puṣkara-piśunita-ddhṛdaya-saṃtāpo roṣa-vaśottambhita-dṛṣṭir guruka-kara-sphoṭita-dharaṇi-mārgo rajanīṣv apy anidrā-sukham anubhūto 'si
children.translated_text: My dear friend! Why do you praise that very wretch of captivity, that son of a slave-woman? Have you forgotten already? How, like a newly captured lordly elephant, stumbling in your chains of clanking iron fetters, the anguish of your heart betrayed by your empty trunk-like face, your gaze stiffened by suppressed rage, your path on the ground pounded by heavy shackles — even in the nights you experienced the pleasure of sleeplessness!

children.text: rājā - Vasantaka durjanaḥ khalv asi | paśya |
children.translated_text: The King — <s>Vasantaka</s>, you are indeed a wicked fellow! Look —

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ cārakam andhakāra-gahanaṃ no tan-mukhendu-dyutiḥ
children.translated_text: You saw the spy in the deep darkness, but not the moonlike radiance of her face;

children.text: pīḍā te nigala-svanena madhurās tasyā giro na śrutāḥ /
children.translated_text: you were pained by the sound of fetters, but did not hear her sweet words;

children.text: krūrā bandhana-rakṣiṇo 'dya manasi snigdhāḥ kaṭākṣā na te
children.translated_text: the cruel prison-guards are in your mind today, but not her tender sidelong glances —

children.text: doṣān paśyasi bandhanasya na punaḥ Pradyota-putryā guṇān // HPri_1.7 //
children.translated_text: you see the faults of captivity, but not the virtues of the daughter of <s>Pradyota</s>! // HPri_1.7 //

children.text: vidūṣakaḥ - (sa-garvam) | bho | jai dāva bandhaṇaṃ suha-ṇibandhaṇaṃ hoi tā kīsa tumaṃ Diḍhavammā baddho tti Kaliṅga-raṇṇo uvari rosaṃ bandhesi |
[bhoḥ | yadi tāvad bandhanaṃ sukha-nibandhanaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: [Sir! If captivity is the cause of happiness,

children.text: tat kasmāt tvaṃ Dṛḍhavarmā baddha iti Kaliṅga-rājasyopari roṣaṃ badhnāsi] |
children.translated_text: then why do you bind anger upon the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s>, saying '<s>Dṛḍhavarman</s> has been imprisoned'?]
<s>Vidūṣaka</s> — (Proudly.) Sir! If captivity is the cause of happiness, then why do you bind anger upon the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s>, saying '<s>Dṛḍhavarman</s> has been imprisoned'?

children.text: rājā - (vihasya) | dhiṅ mūrkha | na khalu sarvo Vatsarājo ya evaṃ Vāsavadattām avāpya bandhanān niryāsyati | tad āstāṃ tāvad iyaṃ kathā | Vindhyaketor upari bahūny ahāni Vijayasenasya preṣitasya na cādyāpi tat-sakāśāt kaścid āgataḥ | tad āhūyatāṃ tāvad amātyo Rumaṇvān | tena saha kiṃcid ālapitum icchāmi |
children.translated_text: The King — (Laughing.) Shame on you, fool! Truly, not every <s>Vatsarāja</s> will win <s>Vāsavadattā</s> and escape from captivity thus! But let this topic rest for now. Many days have passed since <s>Vijayasena</s> was dispatched against <s>Vindhyaketu</s>, and still no one has come from him. Let the minister <s>Rumaṇvān</s> be summoned. I wish to speak with him about something.

children.text:
(praviśya) |
pratīhārī - jedu jedu devvo | eso kkhu Vijaaseṇo amacco Rumaṇṇo vi paḍihāra-bhūmiṃ uvaṭṭhio |
jayatu jayatu devaḥ | eṣa khalu Vijayaseno 'mātyo Rumaṇvān api pratīhāra-bhūmim upasthitau
children.translated_text: Victory, victory to the lord! Here indeed are <s>Vijayasena</s> and minister <s>Rumaṇvān</s>, arrived at the audience-chamber.

(Entering.)
Doorkeeper — Victory, victory to my lord! Here indeed are <s>Vijayasena</s> and minister <s>Rumaṇvān</s>, arrived at the audience-chamber.

children.text: rājā - tvaritaṃ praveśaya tau |
children.translated_text: The King — Admit them both at once.

children.text: pratīhārī - jaṃ devo āṇavedi |
yad deva ājñāpayati
children.translated_text: As the lord commands.

children.text: (iti niṣkrāntā) |
children.translated_text: (She exits.)
Doorkeeper — As my lord commands.

children.text:
(tataḥ praviśati Rumaṇvān Vijayasenaś ca)
Rumaṇvān - (vicintya) |
children.translated_text:
(Then enter <s>Rumaṇvān</s> and <s>Vijayasena</s>.)
<s>Rumaṇvān</s> — (Reflecting.)

children.text: tat kṣanam api niṣkrāntāḥ kṛta-doṣā iva vināpi doṣeṇa /
children.translated_text: Even when they have left for but a moment, as if guilty though guiltless,

children.text: praviśanti śaṅkamānā rāja-kulaṃ prāyaśo bhṛtyāḥ // HPri_1.8 //
children.translated_text: servants generally enter the royal court with apprehension. // HPri_1.8 //

children.text: (upasṛtya) | jayatu devaḥ |
children.translated_text: (Approaching.) Victory to the lord!

children.text: rājā - (āsanaṃ nirdiśya) | Rumaṇvan | ita āsyatām |
children.translated_text: The King — (Indicating a seat.) <s>Rumaṇvān</s>, please be seated here.

children.text:
Rumaṇvān - (sa-smitam upaviśya | eṣa khalu jita-Vindhyaketur Vijayasenaḥ
praṇamati |
(Vijayasenas tathā karoti) |
children.translated_text:
<s>Rumaṇvān</s> — (Sitting down with a smile.) Here is <s>Vijayasena</s>, victor over <s>Vindhyaketu</s>, who bows before you.
(<s>Vijayasena</s> does so.)

children.text: rājā - (sādaraṃ pariṣvajya) | api kuśalī bhavān |
children.translated_text: The King — (Embracing him with affection.) Are you well, sir?

children.text: Vijayasenaḥ - adya svāminaḥ prasādāt |
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayasena</s> — Today, by the grace of my lord.

children.text: rājā - Vijayasena upaviśyatām |
children.translated_text: The King — <s>Vijayasena</s>, please be seated.

children.text: (Vijayasena upaviśati) |
children.translated_text: (<s>Vijayasena</s> sits down.)

children.text: rājā - Vijayasena kathaya Vindhyaketor vṛttāntam |
children.translated_text: The King — <s>Vijayasena</s>, tell me the account of <s>Vindhyaketu</s>.

children.text: Vijayasenaḥ - deva kim aparaṃ kathayāmi | yādṛśaḥ svāmini kupite |
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayasena</s> — My lord, what more shall I say? As is fitting when the master is angered —

children.text: rājā - tathāpi vistarataḥ śrotum icchāmi |
children.translated_text: The King — Nevertheless, I wish to hear the full account.

children.text: Vijayasenaḥ - deva śrūyatām | ito vayaṃ deva-pādādeśād yathādiṣṭena kari-turaga-padāti-dainyena mahāntam apy adhvānaṃ divasa-trayeṇollaṅghya prabhāta-velāyām atarkitā eva Vindhyaketor upari nipatitāḥ smaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayasena</s> — My lord, hear then. From here, by the lord's command, with the appointed force of elephants, cavalry, and infantry — though meager — we crossed even a great distance in three days, and at dawn fell upon <s>Vindhyaketu</s> entirely without warning.

children.text: rājā - tatas tataḥ |
children.translated_text: The King — Then? Then?

children.text: Vijayasenaḥ - tataḥ so 'py asmad-bala-tumula-kalakalākarṇanena pratibuddhaḥ kesarīva Vindhya-kandarān nirgatya Vindhyaketur an-apekṣita-bala-vāhano yathāsaṃnihita katipaya-sahāyaḥ sahasā sva-nāmodghoṣayann asmān abhiyoddhuṃ pravṛttaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayasena</s> — Then he too, roused by the tumultuous uproar of our forces, like a lion emerging from the caves of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains, <s>Vindhyaketu</s>, without waiting for his army and mounts, with only a handful of companions at hand, suddenly crying out his own name, advanced to fight against us.

children.text: rājā - (Rumaṇvantam avalokya sa-smitam) | śobhitaṃ Vindhyaketunā | tatas tataḥ |
children.translated_text: The King — (Looking at <s>Rumaṇvān</s> with a smile.) Well done by <s>Vindhyaketu</s>! Then? Then?

children.text: Vāsavadattā - (sāsram|) bhaavadi adi-ujjuā dāṇiṃ tumaṃ | jassa mae ṇa kajjaṃ tassa mama-kerayeṇa kiṃ kajjaṃ | ajjuāe juttaṃ mama edaṃ ālihiduṃ | sā uṇa ṇa āṇādi ajja vi tārisī ṇa Vāsavadatte tti | tuha uṇa edaṃ Āraṇṇiāe uttantaṃ paccakkhaṃ | tā kahaṃ edaṃ bhaṇāsi | [

children.translated_text: Venerable one, you are too straightforward now. He who has no need of me -- what need has he of what is mine? It was right for my mother to write this to me. But she still does not know that even now such a woman as <s>Vāsavadattā</s> counts for nothing. You, however, have witnessed <s>Āraṇyikā</s>'s situation firsthand. So how can you say this? [

<s>Vidūṣaka</s> - What is impossible about this? Since, to begin with, there is no other man there except hunchbacks, dwarfs, old men, and <s>kañcukīs</s> (chamberlains)! [

<s>Vidūṣaka</s> - Well sir, observe a month-long fast and preserve your life! In this way Queen <s>Caṇḍī</s> (the Fierce One) will be appeased! [
